title: [FR] Configurable Hashing Algorithm/Using MLFlow in FIPS environment
body:
### Willingness to contribute

No. I cannot contribute this feature at this time.

### Proposal Summary

I would like to have some way to configure the hashing algorithm to be used in the backend. I am very new to MLFlow, but testing it out today I noticed I was running into FIPS errors due to the use of MD5 in the `file_store.py` file. Would it be possible to provide a configuration option that would allow users to switch to another algorithm to bypass these issues?



### Motivation

> #### What is the use case for this feature?
The use case would be leveraging MLFlow in a FIPS enabled environment.

> #### Why is this use case valuable to support for MLflow users in general?
This would allow more interested users who are constrained by FIPS to make use of the tool set.

> #### Why is this use case valuable to support for your project(s) or organization?
Our project is unable to disable FIPS at this time, and this limits our ability to use MLFlow in it's current state.

> #### Why is it currently difficult to achieve this use case?
There is no way, at least as far as I know, to get around this limitation without disabling FIPS outright.
 

### Details

The offending line (though there are many more references to md5 in the code):
`md5 = hashlib.md5(dataset_name.encode("utf-8"))`

`CMD ["mlflow", "server", "--host", "0.0.0.0"]`

Just as a quick note, I am running the above container as a pod and trying to communicate with it from another pod in the same cluster.

Here is the code I ran in my 'client' pod to trigger the error I saw:

```
X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(db.data, db.target)

rf = RandomForestRegressor(n_estimators=100, max_depth=6, max_features=3)
rf.fit(X_train, y_train)

predictions = rf.predict(X_test)
```

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
@participant2  Sure thing:
```
FROM docker.io/library/python:3.9

USER root
ENV NON_ROOT_USER=mlflow
ENV NON_ROOT_GID="1000" \
    NON_ROOT_UID="1000" \
    NON_ROOT_HOME_DIR=/home/${NON_ROOT_USER}

RUN groupadd -g $NON_ROOT_GID parser && useradd -m -s $NON_ROOT_HOME_DIR -u $NON_ROOT_UID $NON_ROOT_USER -g $NON_ROOT_GID

USER mlflow
COPY requirements.txt /tmp/requirements.txt
RUN pip3 install -r /tmp/requirements.txt
ENV PATH="$PATH:/home/<user>/.local/bin"
WORKDIR $NON_ROOT_HOME_DIR

CMD ["mlflow", "server", "--host", "0.0.0.0"]
```

I would reproduce the following way:

- Build the container using the Dockerfile above
- Spin up a RHEL 8 machine with FIPS enabled
- Run the container on that FIPS machine
- From the same machine (or another machine RHEL machine with FIPS enabled), run the code I supplied above. I believe it's the 'autolog' feature in particular that trips the error

comments.author: participant3
comments.body: `hashlib.sha256` would work great. It would be awesome if that could be switched via a flag or environment variable.

comments.author: participant2
participant2
comments.body:
or can we use `usedforsecurity=False`? https://docs.python.org/3/library/hashlib.html#constructors says:

> Changed in version 3.9: All hashlib constructors take a keyword-only argument usedforsecurity with default value True. A false value allows the use of insecure and blocked hashing algorithms in restricted environments. False indicates that the hashing algorithm is not used in a security context, e.g. as a non-cryptographic one-way compression function.

In MLflow, we're not using md5 in a security context.
